text: This is a chemical reaction, replayed from a real simulation, femtosecond by femtosecond.
A chloride ion closes in on methyl bromide, always from the side opposite the bromine.
As the new carbon–chlorine bond forms, the old carbon–bromine bond stretches.

text: At the top of the energy barrier, the carbon is shared, and its three hydrogens lie flat.
Then they flip, like an umbrella in the wind, and bromide is pushed out.
One step, one inversion. That is an SN2 reaction.
tts: One step, one inversion. That is an S N two reaction.
